per_row_oracle_pick.note: ORACLE, uses labels to pick the best member per row; not achievable

findings: The champion is exactly a fixed four-member convex blend with weights 0.30 on D and 0.70/3 on each model member, reproduced to 1.1e-11 kWh.

ORACLE convex re-weighting, with the weights chosen directly on the outer evaluation folds, reaches only 0.6330387 against the deployed 0.6314827. The entire fixed-weight ensemble axis is worth at most +0.001556, which is 5.5 percent of the 0.0285173 gap.
Therefore FD13 is closed as a source of the remaining gap: no fixed re-weighting of these four action vectors can approach 0.660000, even with the answers.

By contrast, an ORACLE per-row selection of the single best of the four members reaches 0.7255569, which is 0.0940741 above the champion. The members are genuinely diverse; the information is present but is not reachable by any fixed weight.

The productive axis is therefore CONDITIONAL combination: a past-only gate that predicts, per row, which member or which local weighting is right. Capturing about 30 percent of the oracle per-row headroom would clear the target.
residual_deficit: FD14: the champion combines members unconditionally while the member-optimality signal is strongly row-dependent. No past-only gate has ever been fitted or tested locally.
oracle_disclosure: The convex ceiling and the per-row pick both use outer-fold labels. They are ceilings and diagnostics only; neither is a selection and neither may be promoted.
